strings.AGL_Reluctant_Revolution_desc:
The policymakers of Anguilla were not keen on moving their organization away from the Leeward Islands, yet neither could the people stomach a blatant contempt from those who rested upon the ivory tower. While most other so-called revolutions tend to be the products of international meddling, the secession of the island from its brethren was reluctant, yet an inevitable consequence of a decade-long negligence that had pushed the masses to the brink.

Despite being diplomatically isolated following its de facto independence, desperation had brought out a revolutionary spirit which the people themselves knew not they had. Hope for development burns brighter than ever despite ostracism from her peers, for so long as the nation stands, no hardship will be too great to endure.
